top.title: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’
top.description: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’ After a season in which he appeared below his best level, Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham appears to have returned to his peak this campaign. One of the main objectives for manager Jose Mourinho when he took over the reins in the summer was to help the England international regain his mojo after a year disrupted by injuries, confusion over his role, and inconsistent displays. And, judging by how things have been going, it is safe to say that the 23-year-old is once again looking like one of the most influential players in the world. The latest display of his quality came on Saturday when he helped Real Madrid secure a 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu, scoring the equalising goal in the second half. Alvaro Benito left stunned by Bellingham Following the match, former Real Madrid player Alvaro Benito was effusive in praise of Bellingham, stating that the England star was enjoying his best moment at the club and was the best in the world in his position. Bellingham starred for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “We are witnessing the best version of Bellingham. He has an influence on the game that he didn’t have before; now he’s a complete player,” Benito said on Cadena SER (h/t AS ). He also highlighted the mentality that separates Bellingham from other players, saying: “For me, he’s the best midfielder in the world; he’s capable of doing everything. Of all his virtues, the greatest is his ambition and his winning, competitive mentality. For me, without a doubt, this is Bellingham’s best moment at Real Madrid.” Vinicius and other teammates join in praise Bellingham, for his goal and overall contributions last night, was named the Man of the Match against Celta Vigo. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jude Bellingham (@judebellingham) Following the match, the Real Madrid superstar shared a post on Instagram, prompting several of his teammates to respond with messages of admiration. Vinicius Jr. wrote: “You’re the best,” while youngster Thiago Pitarch added: “Another level.” Real Madrid’s other hero against Celta Vigo, Carlos Espi, responded: “What a show.” Injured forward Rodrygo also joined in, writing: “What a player.” The result also saw Bellingham achieve a special milestone as he recorded his 100th La Liga victory with Real Madrid. Given his impact and influence, it does not come as a surprise to see Real Madrid working to extend Bellingham’s contract until 2032 .

top.title: Colorado’s 380-pound guard Chauncey Gooden took down more than a Cincinnati player defending a teammate
top.description: The Colorado Buffaloes saw their bowl hopes end Saturday with a 35-28 loss to the Cincinnati Bearcats at Nippert Stadium, and one of the afternoon’s most-shared clips belonged to a 380-pound offensive lineman. Late in the game, Cincinnati’s Antwan Peek Jr. stood over a Colorado receiver who was down after a play. As an official moved in to pull Peek away, Chauncey Gooden charged in and took down both Peek and the official. Players from both teams rushed in before officials separated them, and Deion Sanders stepped into the scrum to send his players away. Chauncey Gooden got his teammates back https://t.co/O9WFxWnIwC — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 21, 2026 Coach Prime Had To Get In Between Colorado Players And Cincinnati Players After The Game. Isaac Wilson threw three interceptions, and Cole Tabb scored four touchdowns as Cincinnati became bowl eligible and won in November for the first time since 2024 after 12 straight losses in the month. Travel problems the day before the game had put the Buffaloes behind before they arrived. Apr 11, 2026; Boulder, CO, USA; Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders before the start of the spring game at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images “Early in the game, we didn’t show up. We were still on the tarmac. Early turnovers crippled us,” Sanders said. He put the rest of the result on himself. “We just have no true consistency. We don’t know at this point how we’re going to show up. Is the offense going to show up, the defense going to show up, the special teams. All of it’s on me,” Sanders said . Who is Chauncey Gooden? Gooden is a second-year guard from Nashville who played at Lipscomb Academy and has started every game he has appeared in this season. After an Aug. 10 practice, assistant offensive line coach George Hegamin said there was “a lot more aggression and a lot more violence up front” and named Gooden as the lineman who brings that intent. A week before the trip to Cincinnati, Gooden was part of the line, with Xavier Payne, Sean Kinney, Leon Bell and Larry Johnson III, named the Big 12 Offensive Line of the Week after the Buffaloes ran 39 times for 249 yards and five touchdowns without allowing a sack in the win over Houston. Colorado managed 67 rushing yards in the first half and 121 for the game, and the loss dropped the Buffaloes to 4-7, guaranteeing a third losing season in Sanders’ four years in Boulder and a second straight year without a bowl. It was also Colorado’s 10th straight loss in Big 12 road games. In a season with little left to play for, Gooden’s most visible moment in Cincinnati came after a play was over, standing up for a teammate on the turf. top.description: The Tennessee Volunteers beat the LSU Tigers 27-13 at Neyland Stadium on Saturday night, and with 3:14 left, the game stopped because of what came out of the stands. After a pass interference call gave LSU a first down at the Tennessee 30, fans threw golf balls, mustard bottles and other debris onto the field, and LSU’s players left their sideline until it was cleared. The objects were the same ones that rained down in October 2021, the last time Lane Kiffin brought a visiting team to Knoxville. His Ole Miss Rebels won 31-26 that night, Kiffin was hit by a golf ball, and University of Tennessee police reported 18 arrests and 47 ejections. The SEC fined Tennessee $250,000 , and the school banned 16 students and nine other fans from its athletic events. top.title: Kirk Ferentz makes feelings on CFP committee clear after Iowa’s 34-17 win at Illinois
top.description: The Iowa Hawkeyes beat the Illinois Fighting Illini 34-17 in Champaign on Saturday to move to 9-2 without leading rusher Kamari Moulton, who is out for the season, taking control early and answering every time Illinois scored. Kirk Ferentz had barely left the field when Big Ten Network sideline reporter Brooke Fletcher asked what a win like that could show the College Football Playoff selection committee. Iowa came into the weekend at No. 15 in the committee’s rankings, the same spot it held a week earlier. A 28-7 win over the Purdue Boilermakers, Iowa’s third straight Big Ten win by a combined 82-17 , had left the Hawkeyes in place while the Oregon Ducks and Ohio State Buckeyes moved past them. Nov 11, 2023; Iowa City, Iowa, USA; Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz reacts during the fourth quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Kinnick Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care. Our goal is to come in here and win. It’s not easy winning in college football. It’s not easy on the road, conference game, so go right down the list, so I’m just really happy for our guys,” Ferentz told Fletcher. “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care.” Iowa’s Kirk Ferentz on the CFP committee https://t.co/4LHs8zTIK4 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 21, 2026 Iowa beat Purdue by three touchdowns and held it to a single score, and the win did nothing for its ranking. The questions about style points followed the team to Illinois anyway. A committee that left a 28-7 Big Ten win unrewarded gives Ferentz little reason to chase margins now. Iowa’s two losses include a rivalry defeat that still shapes how its season is judged. The Minnesota Golden Gophers beat the Hawkeyes 13-10 on a field goal as time expired on Oct. 24, a game in which Iowa turned the ball over four times and changed quarterbacks, with Hank Brown replacing Jeremy Hecklinski in the second quarter. Iowa has won every game since. What can still move Iowa into the playoff field? No. 4 UCLA fell 18-16 in triple overtime at Michigan, the Indiana Hoosiers lost, and Ohio State, one of the two teams that jumped Iowa last week, fell 31-28 at Nebraska for its fourth loss of the season. Those results did more for Iowa than its own score. That Nebraska Cornhuskers team comes to Kinnick Stadium for Iowa’s regular-season finale on Friday, Nov. 27, at noon ET. A week ago, beating Nebraska would have looked like a routine rivalry win to close the season. It now means beating the team that just ended Ohio State’s playoff hopes, which gives Iowa’s resume something the committee can point to without Ferentz ever making the argument himself. top.title: What Bob Chesney told UCLA players in the locker room after triple-overtime loss to Michigan
top.description: Bob Chesney had gone 10 games at UCLA without addressing a losing locker room. That ended Saturday night at Michigan Stadium, where the Michigan Wolverines beat the No. 4 UCLA Bruins 18-16 in three overtimes and cost them a chance to clinch a spot in the Big Ten championship game. UCLA scored one touchdown all night, with 10 seconds left in regulation. Ty Dieffenbach threw an interception in the red zone in the first quarter and was strip-sacked while the Bruins were driving late in the first half. One of his two lost fumbles set up Michigan’s go-ahead touchdown early in the fourth quarter. In overtime, UCLA settled for two field goals before Madden Iamaleava’s two-point pass fell incomplete in the third period. Oct 17, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney in the first half against the Wisconsin Badgers at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short, and like we always say, we have to find a way to get better, period. That’s it, no excuses. I thought they played a really good game of football. We know they were tough. “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team, and you battled with that team, and then we came up a little short. “When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it,” Chesney said . Bob Chesney on UCLA’s loss at Michigan: “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team & you battled… When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it.” https://t.co/3UDwFXMq1O — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 22, 2026 The 16 points were UCLA’s lowest total of the season. Chesney said afterward that the Bruins cannot give the ball away the way they did near the goal line, where the turnovers took points off the board. A defense that held Michigan to one touchdown in regulation gave UCLA enough to win. Who will play quarterback for UCLA against USC? The answer depends on Dieffenbach, who was carted off after a 6-yard run on the first play of overtime. Chesney had no update on the injury after the game. Dieffenbach had taken over as the starter after Nico Iamaleava’s season-ending knee injury in October, which leaves Madden Iamaleava, Nico’s younger brother, as the next option. “It’s tough to lose anybody. It’s the brand, the game that we play. We all understand that it’s really hard to make it through the whole season unscathed. Not the greatest moment to lose him. But at the same point, we have to trust Madden. He’s got to be able to deliver in those moments,” Chesney said . top.title: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus
top.description: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus Stefan Leitl’s side arrived at the LEAG Energie Stadion looking to build on their impressive 2-1 victory over promotion rivals Wolfsburg before the international break, and they made the perfect start to the Berlin-Brandenburg derby. The visitors needed just six minutes to break the deadlock, with Sebastian Grønning rising highest to head home Mads Pedersen’s corner from close range. Cottbus attempted to respond, with Justin Butler testing Marius Gersbeck from distance, while the hosts were briefly awarded a penalty in the 23rd minute after Deyovaisio Zeefuik appeared to handle inside the area. However, referee Florian Exner overturned his initial decision following a VAR review, ruling that the Hertha defender’s arm had been in a natural position. Energie thought they had found an equaliser shortly afterwards when Lucas Copado found the net following a set-piece, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Despite Cottbus showing some resistance, Hertha remained in control and almost doubled their advantage before the interval when Grønning was denied from close range by Marcel Lotka. The visitors did not have to wait long after the restart to extend their lead. Just three minutes into the second half, Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson flicked on a corner at the near post, allowing Paul Seguin to arrive unmarked and head home from close range. Cottbus’ hopes of mounting a comeback were dealt another significant blow in the 58th minute when Fousseny Doumbia was shown a straight red card for bringing down Thorsteinsson as the last defender. With a numerical advantage, Hertha were able to manage the remainder of the contest with relative comfort, Kevin Sessa came close to adding a third when his follow-up effort flew over the crossbar. The visitors eventually put the result beyond doubt in the closing stages, with Deyovaisio Zeefuik making it 3-0 in the 90th minute before substitute Gustaf Nilsson completed the scoring moments later. The Swedish forward’s strike was particularly memorable, marking his first goal for Hertha since joining the club. The emphatic victory means Hertha remain unbeaten after 12 league matches, having collected 34 points from a possible 36. They now hold a ten-point advantage over second-placed Nürnberg and are firmly establishing themselves as the early favourites for promotion. Cottbus, meanwhile, remain without a victory in their last seven league matches and sit 17th in the table with 11 points, continuing their difficult run since the start of the campaign.

top.title: “What the Unemployed Sound Like”: Landry Kiffin Gives Brutal Reply to Tennessee Crowd for Going After Dad Lane Kiffin
top.description: Sep 27, 2025; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin poses for a photo with his daughter Landry Kiffin prior to the game against the LSU Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. © Petre Thomas-Imagn Images It wasn’t a happy return to his old stomping grounds for Lane Kiffin as LSU was humbled 27-13 by Tennessee in Knoxville, and the fans’ hatred for their former head coach was visible as they created a raucous atmosphere inside Neyland stadium. Vols fans took over the game at multiple times, making their feelings about Kiffin known as they tossed objects onto the field, including golf balls, mustard bottles and other trash, and after the game, Lane Kiffin’s daughter Landry Kiffin’s support for her dad became public. Landry posted on social media platform TikTok about her experience with the fans, referring to them as “unemployed” as she walked around the stadium. “Rent free,” Landry captioned the video, as also posted by Jack Mac . “In case you’re wondering what the unemployed sound like,” she also wrote. Lane Kiffin Spoke About the Impact of the Crowd After the Game Lane Kiffin acknowledged that the crowd played a major role in his team being unable to get going against Tennessee. When asked about what LSU does in training to battle something like this, Kiffin explained his usual exercise. “I mean, we put the speakers right behind us and everything. And so again, we’ve been doing this for years and I just think that they somehow hit a level that’s louder. Plus, some players have louder claps. Quarterbacks over time,” Kiffin remarked in the postgame press conference. He further said he doesn’t feel it’ll be an issue going forward, but doesn’t want to motivate Arkansas, LSU’s next opponents. “I don’t think it’ll be an issue. I don’t want to motivate Arkansas, but I don’t think it’ll be an issue. They’re the same. Otherwise if you could redo it, you know, you’d look at different, you know, cadence from the offensive line.” The loss means LSU’s record stands at 6-5 now, and they need to pick up a win against Arkansas in the team’s next clash on Saturday. top.title: Sun Belt Week 12 Takeaways: Nearing the End
top.description: Photo credit: Marshall Athletics | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor With the 2026 college football regular season coming to an end, the Sun Belt Conference saw several teams effectively play for their seasons. Some games ended in blowouts, while one went down to the final seconds. Bowl eligibility and division leads were on the line. Let’s see how this week went for teams with a lot to play for. Sun Belt Week 12 Recap Georgia State at Marshall This matchup between Georgia State and Marshall was huge for both teams’ bowl eligibility aspirations. Let’s say both teams came to play, and this one went all the way down to the wire. The Thundering Herd ended up escaping with the victory over the Panthers, 28-27. Down seven with 10 seconds left, Ayden Pereira found Rodshaun Dorsey on a Hail Mary in the back of the end zone for the touchdown. Unfortunately for the Panthers, they missed the extra point to tie the game, leading to a tough loss. Quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson started his first game for the Thundering Herd since Oct. 10. While he only completed 12 of 23 passes, he did throw three touchdowns and ran for an additional touchdown. The Thundering Herd gained bowl eligibility with this victory and head into next week’s game against Louisiana-Monroe with considerably less pressure. For the Panthers, there were some very good things that they showcased in this one, specifically on offense. Pereira had a much better showing than last week, and the run game was productive. The one mistake the Panthers would love to take back is the interception at the end of the first half by Pereira. top.description: Jul 29, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees relief pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) reacts as he walks off the field after the top of the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. Mark Feinsand reported Friday for MLB.com that the right-hander agreed to return on a two-year deal worth about $18 million, with a club option for 2029. The report said the deal was pending a physical; the Yankees had not announced it. I’d make that deal, with one caveat. Let Loaisiga start clean innings. Don’t make the entire middle of the bullpen depend on his ability to work on short rest and escape somebody else’s trouble. He didn’t get there by blowing everybody away. Feinsand’s report put his strikeout rate at 18.4% and his walk rate at 5%. Baseball Savant’s contact profile shows why that combination worked: 55.8% ground balls and a 3.5% barrel rate. Those numbers matter in a clean seventh. Loaisiga can attack the first hitter instead of having to make a perfect pitch with a runner already in scoring position. If a hitter rolls over his sinker, he can get an out without getting deep into the count. He can also use a changeup off the sinker when a hitter is ready to swing at the harder pitch. It is a practical way to get three outs without trying to win every at-bat with a strikeout. The success wasn’t confined to one good month. Across his last 30 regular-season appearances he walked six in 32 2/3 innings. He also threw two scoreless innings against the Yankees on September 20. The Yankees should still have an option for an inherited-runner spot where a strikeout is particularly valuable. top.title: Blackburn rally without Tony Mowbray to deny Burnley long-awaited home win
top.description: Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues . In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted. Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season. Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message ‘We’re with you, Tony’ on the back and the number 900 on the front. Blackburn honoured Tony Mowbray before kick-off (PA) Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute. Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead. The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react. But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a T-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras. Andri Gudjohnsen paid tribute to Mowbray while celebrating his equaliser (PA) Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off. The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio. Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2. Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

nigeria.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
nigeria.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. nigeria.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
nigeria.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. nigeria.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
nigeria.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts. The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it. She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added. Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation. nigeria.title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
nigeria.description: … 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products. The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed. The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026. The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria. The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security. In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool. It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App. The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products. NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking. Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026. The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation. NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa. nigeria.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety measures on the nation’s waterways to prevent further loss of lives. Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them. In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning. He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred. “What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said. “Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities.” Ologbondiyan commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations. He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices. He said preventing similar accidents would require sustained government investment in safer water transportation. “The Federal and State Governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stressed. “For millions of Nigerians in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, water transportation is not a luxury; it is a daily necessity. Their safety must never be treated as an afterthought.” He also urged the Federal Government, Bayelsa State Government and relevant humanitarian agencies to provide immediate assistance to survivors and bereaved families. Such assistance, he said, should include medical care, psychosocial support and financial help with the burial of victims. Atiku commiserated with the bereaved families, the people of Ayama and Ukubie communities and the Bayelsa State Government, while praying for the repose of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured. nigeria.title: PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL
nigeria.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday. Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered off in tears. The French international will undergo surgery before the end of the month, PSG added in a brief statement, without specifying the expected length of his absence, which is likely to be a matter of months. Doue looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow him to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG have also lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “It is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said on Saturday night. The French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. nigeria.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
nigeria.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State. According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community. Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians. The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate. Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition. She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour. The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests. “We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence. “I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty. “I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general. “Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said. Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake. In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved. He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people. nigeria.title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
nigeria.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. sports.description: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus Stefan Leitl’s side arrived at the LEAG Energie Stadion looking to build on their impressive 2-1 victory over promotion rivals Wolfsburg before the international break, and they made the perfect start to the Berlin-Brandenburg derby. The visitors needed just six minutes to break the deadlock, with Sebastian Grønning rising highest to head home Mads Pedersen’s corner from close range. Cottbus attempted to respond, with Justin Butler testing Marius Gersbeck from distance, while the hosts were briefly awarded a penalty in the 23rd minute after Deyovaisio Zeefuik appeared to handle inside the area. However, referee Florian Exner overturned his initial decision following a VAR review, ruling that the Hertha defender’s arm had been in a natural position. Energie thought they had found an equaliser shortly afterwards when Lucas Copado found the net following a set-piece, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Despite Cottbus showing some resistance, Hertha remained in control and almost doubled their advantage before the interval when Grønning was denied from close range by Marcel Lotka. The visitors did not have to wait long after the restart to extend their lead. Just three minutes into the second half, Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson flicked on a corner at the near post, allowing Paul Seguin to arrive unmarked and head home from close range. Cottbus’ hopes of mounting a comeback were dealt another significant blow in the 58th minute when Fousseny Doumbia was shown a straight red card for bringing down Thorsteinsson as the last defender. With a numerical advantage, Hertha were able to manage the remainder of the contest with relative comfort, Kevin Sessa came close to adding a third when his follow-up effort flew over the crossbar. The visitors eventually put the result beyond doubt in the closing stages, with Deyovaisio Zeefuik making it 3-0 in the 90th minute before substitute Gustaf Nilsson completed the scoring moments later. The Swedish forward’s strike was particularly memorable, marking his first goal for Hertha since joining the club. The emphatic victory means Hertha remain unbeaten after 12 league matches, having collected 34 points from a possible 36. They now hold a ten-point advantage over second-placed Nürnberg and are firmly establishing themselves as the early favourites for promotion. Cottbus, meanwhile, remain without a victory in their last seven league matches and sit 17th in the table with 11 points, continuing their difficult run since the start of the campaign.

Loaisiga can attack the first hitter instead of having to make a perfect pitch with a runner already in scoring position. If a hitter rolls over his sinker, he can get an out without getting deep into the count. He can also use a changeup off the sinker when a hitter is ready to swing at the harder pitch. sports.description: Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues . In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted. Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react. Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. sports.title: Maple Leafs 2027 1st Rounder Continues to Rise; It’s Time for the League to Step In and Decide: Flyers or Bruins?
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For all intents and purposes, the Toronto Maple Leafs traded the same first-round draft pick twice at the 2025 NHL Trade Deadline. Two trade deadlines ago, the Maple Leafs were in the hunt and were wheeling and dealing, trying to push their roster over the edge for a run at the Stanley Cup. It started by trading their 2027 First-round pick, top-10 protected, to the Philadelphia Flyers, alongside Nikita Grebenkin , in exchange for center Scott Laughton . Then, as a buzzer-beater at the deadline, they traded their 2026 first-rounder, top-5 protected, along with prospect Fraser Minten , to the Boston Bruins for defenseman Brandon Carlo. At the time, everything seemed fine. But the 2026 NHL Draft Lottery has sent the league into a bit of a spiral. The Maple Leafs won the lottery, selecting 1st overall in the 2026 NHL Draft, which fell under protection. The problem? Both the Flyers and Bruins feel entitled to the Leafs 2027 first-rounder, which currently has the 4th-best odds at the top pick. If the Leafs’ pick somehow falls outside of the top-10, it becomes easy: the Flyers receive that pick. However, if it falls inside of the protection, then things can get murky. Should the Flyers be entitled to the pick since their trade was completed first? Or should the Bruins receive the 2027 pick because they received the earlier 2026 draft pick? Before the 2026 NHL Draft Lottery, we wrote what our friends at Puckpedia had reported : if the Leafs’ 2026 pick is protected, then they would have to choose who receives the 2027 pick if it’s inside the top 10. On Sportsnet’s Saturday night headlines , NHL insider Elliotte Friedman shared the same thing. “If it is in the top 10, as it stands now, Toronto chooses which team gets it, and the other team would get the unprotected 2028 first.” “We’ve been trying to get some clarity from the league,” Friedman added. “Does this stand? Is this the way it’s actually going to go? And the answer is yes. In the eyes of the NHL, the way that the trade information is put together, it’s quite clear that it’s Toronto’s choice. So the Maple Leafs do have the option of which team to pick.” That is going to create a tricky scenario to navigate for the Flyers and the Bruins. It’s time for the league to step in. technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight.
